o: The apostle prefaces his epistle to believers in general, with evident testimonies to Christ, for promoting their happiness and joy.
The necessity of a life of holiness, in order to communion with God, is shown.
bg: The fourth of the catholic or "general" epistles. It was evidently written by John the evangelist, and probably also at Ephesus, and when the writer was in advanced age.
ch.s: This chapter covers: The apostle prefaces his epistle to believers in general, with evident testimonies to Christ, for promoting their happiness and joy (vv. 1–4); The necessity of a life of holiness, in order to communion with God, is shown (vv. 5–10).
ch.mh: That essential Good, that uncreated Excellence, which had been from the beginning, from eternity, as equal with the Father, and which at length appeared in human nature for the salvation of sinners, was the great subject concerning which the apostle wrote to his brethren.
q: Read verses 1–4 (The apostle prefaces his epistle to believers in general, with evident testimonies to Christ, for promoting their happiness and joy). What is happening, and what stands out to you most?
In verses 5–10 (The necessity of a life of holiness, in order to communion with God, is shown), what do you learn about truth and light?
Verse 7 is one of the most cross-referenced verses in this chapter. Read it alongside Ephesians 5:8. How do the two passages shed light on each other?
Where do you see the theme of sin and repentance in this chapter, and how does it connect to the rest of 1 John?
What is one specific way you can put this chapter into practice this week?
ch.aq: Let us honestly confess all our sins in their full extent, relying wholly on his mercy and truth through the righteousness of Christ, for a free and full forgiveness, and our deliverance from the power and practice of sin.
ch.a: Ask God to search your heart, confess what He shows you, and make any right amends.

o: The apostle directs to the atonement of Christ for help against sinful infirmities.
The effects of saving knowledge in producing obedience, and love to the brethren.
Christians addressed as little children, young men, and fathers.
All are cautioned against the love of this world, and against errors.
They are encouraged to stand fast in faith and holiness.
bg: The fourth of the catholic or "general" epistles. It was evidently written by John the evangelist, and probably also at Ephesus, and when the writer was in advanced age.
ch.s: This chapter covers: The apostle directs to the atonement of Christ for help against sinful infirmities (vv. 1,2); The effects of saving knowledge in producing obedience, and love to the brethren (vv. 3–11); Christians addressed as little children, young men, and fathers (vv. 12–14); All are cautioned against the love of this world, and against errors (vv. 15–23); They are encouraged to stand fast in faith and holiness (vv. 24–29).
ch.mh: When have an Advocate with the Father; one who has undertaken, and is fully able, to plead in behalf of every one who applies for pardon and salvation in his name, depending on his pleading for them.
q: Read verses 1,2 (The apostle directs to the atonement of Christ for help against sinful infirmities). What is happening, and what stands out to you most?
In verses 3–11 (The effects of saving knowledge in producing obedience, and love to the brethren), what do you learn about truth and light?
Verse 15 is one of the most cross-referenced verses in this chapter. Read it alongside James 4:4. How do the two passages shed light on each other?
Where do you see the theme of family and generations in this chapter, and how does it connect to the rest of 1 John?
What is one specific way you can put this chapter into practice this week?
ch.aq: Then, let us beware of holding the truth in unrighteousness, remembering that those only are born of God, who bear his holy image, and walk in his most righteous ways.
ch.a: Choose one clear command in this chapter and put it into practice before the week ends.

o: The apostle admires the love of God in making believers his children.
The purifying influence of the hope of seeing Christ, and the danger of pretending to this, and living in sin.
Love to the brethren is the character of real Christians.
That love described by its actings.
The advantage of faith, love, and obedience.
bg: The fourth of the catholic or "general" epistles. It was evidently written by John the evangelist, and probably also at Ephesus, and when the writer was in advanced age.
A possession; a spear. (1.) The first-born son of Adam and Eve (Gen. 4). He became a tiller of the ground, as his brother Abel followed the pursuits of pastoral life.
ch.s: This chapter covers: The apostle admires the love of God in making believers his children (vv. 1,2); The purifying influence of the hope of seeing Christ, and the danger of pretending to this, and living in sin (vv. 3–10); Love to the brethren is the character of real Christians (vv. 11–15); That love described by its actings (vv. 16–21); The advantage of faith, love, and obedience (vv. 22–24). People named: Cain.
ch.mh: Little does the world know of the happiness of the real followers of Christ.
q: Read verses 1,2 (The apostle admires the love of God in making believers his children). What is happening, and what stands out to you most?
In verses 3–10 (The purifying influence of the hope of seeing Christ, and the danger of pretending to this, and living in sin), what do you learn about sin and repentance?
Verse 1 is one of the most cross-referenced verses in this chapter. Read it alongside John 1:12. How do the two passages shed light on each other?
What does Cain’s part in this chapter teach you — as an example to follow or a warning to heed?
Where do you see the theme of love in this chapter, and how does it connect to the rest of 1 John?
What is one specific way you can put this chapter into practice this week?
ch.aq: Surely we should love those whom God has loved, and so loved.
ch.a: Ask God to search your heart, confess what He shows you, and make any right amends.

o: Believers cautioned against giving heed to every one that pretends to the Spirit.
bg: The fourth of the catholic or "general" epistles. It was evidently written by John the evangelist, and probably also at Ephesus, and when the writer was in advanced age.
ch.s: This chapter covers: Believers cautioned against giving heed to every one that pretends to the Spirit (vv. 1–6); Brotherly love enforced (vv. 7–21). Places: No.
ch.mh: Christians who are well acquainted with the Scriptures, may, in humble dependence on Divine teaching, discern those who set forth doctrines according to the apostles, and those who contradict them.
q: Read verses 1–6 (Believers cautioned against giving heed to every one that pretends to the Spirit). What is happening, and what stands out to you most?
In verses 7–21 (Brotherly love enforced), what do you learn about love?
Verse 4 is one of the most cross-referenced verses in this chapter. Read it alongside Romans 8:31. How do the two passages shed light on each other?
Where do you see the theme of the holy spirit in this chapter, and how does it connect to the rest of 1 John?
What is one specific way you can put this chapter into practice this week?
ch.aq: But if it is plain that our natural enmity is changed into affection and gratitude, let us bless the name of our God for this seal and earnest of eternal happiness.
ch.a: Do one concrete, unannounced act of love for someone in your home or church.

o: Brotherly love is the effect of the new birth, which makes obedience to all God's commandments pleasant.
Reference to witnesses agreeing to prove that Jesus, the Son of God, is the true Messiah.
The satisfaction the believer has about Christ, and eternal life through him.
The assurance of God's hearing and answering prayer.
The happy condition of true believers, and a charge to renounce all idolatry.
bg: The fourth of the catholic or "general" epistles. It was evidently written by John the evangelist, and probably also at Ephesus, and when the writer was in advanced age.
ch.s: This chapter covers: Brotherly love is the effect of the new birth, which makes obedience to all God's commandments pleasant (vv. 1–5); Reference to witnesses agreeing to prove that Jesus, the Son of God, is the true Messiah (vv. 6–8); The satisfaction the believer has about Christ, and eternal life through him (vv. 9–12); The assurance of God's hearing and answering prayer (vv. 13–17); The happy condition of true believers, and a charge to renounce all idolatry (vv. 18–21).
ch.mh: True love for the people of God, may be distinguished from natural kindness or party attachments, by its being united with the love of God, and obedience to his commands.
q: Read verses 1–5 (Brotherly love is the effect of the new birth, which makes obedience to all God's commandments pleasant). What is happening, and what stands out to you most?
In verses 6–8 (Reference to witnesses agreeing to prove that Jesus, the Son of God, is the true Messiah), what do you learn about faith and trust?
Verse 14 is one of the most cross-referenced verses in this chapter. Read it alongside John 14:13. How do the two passages shed light on each other?
Where do you see the theme of sin and repentance in this chapter, and how does it connect to the rest of 1 John?
What is one specific way you can put this chapter into practice this week?
ch.aq: And let us be truly thankful that no sin, of which any one truly repents, is unto death.
ch.a: Name one worry and deliberately hand it over to God in prayer each day this week.
